_comment: Benchmark a REAL Canton Network Token Standard (CIP-0056) registry.
The measured operation is the standard interface choice itself —
on splice-api-token-transfer-instruction-v1, exercised against a registry
that implements the real Holding and TransferFactory interfaces from the
prebuilt Splice DARs. This is the transaction a wallet actually submits.
setup    one TransferFactory (the registry), then a pool of holdings for
measured each transfer spends one holding through the factory, which
archives the input and creates receiver + change holdings.
The factory choice is NONCONSUMING (verified live), so the factory is a
shared, reusable contract every transfer touches — the question this run
answers is whether that, or the holding pool, is what limits throughput.

setup._comment: The registry's transfer factory. `users` are the parties allowed to submit transfers against it.
The sending wallet's holdings. One per measured transfer, so a transfer normally has its own input to spend.

_comment: The standard transfer. Exercised on the interface id, not on our
template — exactly as an interoperating wallet would do it.
